content: Saga: sequence of local transactions, each a separate service, with compensations on failure. Choreography = services publish/consume events and decide locally; low coupling, good for simple/high-volume flows, but ordering and end-to-end testing get hard as steps grow (need running instances of every service or heavy mocking). Orchestration = central orchestrator issues commands and tracks state; easier to test in isolation (mock the orchestrator), better for workflows with strict ordering/branching, but the orchestrator is a coupling point and potential bottleneck. Common real-world answer: hybrid - simple flows choreographed, complex/branchy flows orchestrated.
